title: The Cat in the Mural
text: “I guess it wasn’t so much that they went extinct as that they set off somewhere… but where could they have gone?”
“That’s a new interpretation, Mother.”
“Indeed. To think such a fact could exist.”

By the time we reached the very end of the dungeon, the queen had come to see it herself, I say. Being someone whose hobby was investigating historical mysteries, her eyes lit up at the findings, and she threw herself into researching them.
“Heroes, I would be grateful if you could come closer to that mural over there as well. It has caught my attention.”
“Yeah, yeah. Got it.”

Itsuki approached the mural. There, depicted, was what looked like a cat-type demi-human with a lizard-like tail, standing shoulder to shoulder with peckuls and the heroes. At the edges, two whale-like creatures were drawn. This mural… I recalled seeing something similar in Filolial-sama’s sanctuary.
“How should I put it… it looks kind of like a commemorative photo. Like something to mark a grand opening.”
“It doesn’t seem far off, does it?”
“Yeah. It looks exactly like the kind of composition you’d find in some tourist information center.”

Ren and Itsuki stared at the mural with rather complicated expressions. As for the equipment, it turned out to be something capable of adjusting the breeding of monsters on the island and interfering with matters related to the climate. Among the equipment, we also found something called a peckul gene. According to Doctor, by using the factors stored in this gene, one could reproduce creatures close to peckuls. Father and the others theorized that by Class Up-ing raised monsters to bring them closer to peckuls, one could apply a buff that strengthened peckuls using the sacred weapon’s skills. And so, having finished our investigation of the island, we returned to being human once more and resumed our daily lives in the village. That night, back in the village, we were all having dinner in the village dining hall, chatting idly.
“What an ordeal. Making us go all the way to the end and then that.”
“Indeed.”

Ren and Itsuki were still grumbling about the dungeon, as usual. Though calling it a wasted effort would hardly be fair, given the massive haul of rare items, experience points, and weapons we’d gotten out of it.
“Itsuki, want to head to Dracia Mountain Range next time we’re off? I bet there’s some trick in there designed to mock us!”

“Nosferatu Great Forest sounds good too. And Prado Desert. Now that it’s come to this, let’s find out just how far we can go—maybe even complete it! And if the creator’s hiding somewhere in one of these dungeons, they’re going to pay for it! We’ll paint the town red with a real riska’s blood!”
“How should I put this… I feel like you two are getting a little too into this…”

Father remarked with a wry smile at the pair. Incidentally, thanks to learning a spell that let him transform into a peckul, Father had apparently been swimming in the sea with Older Sister. He’d also been going on walks with Panda, and inspecting aspects of the village only visible while in peckul form. As for me, I had Father—in his human form—groom my fur while I was in usaunny form, I say! I finally understood how Filo-tan, Filolial-sama, the Raph-species, and Keel must feel when Father pets them!
“It seems the heroes are living quite fulfilling lives, nano.”
“We are not fulfilled! We’re only conquering this out of pure spite! We’re going to unravel every mystery this world has to offer!”
“Such boundless adventurous spirit, nano.”
“I guess it means there are probably other hidden dungeons out there too. There’s likely more to find.”
Indeed. It wasn’t hard to imagine that there were other dungeons and treasures out there that people speculated the Crimson Swine’s true body might have crushed.
“In a way, it could end up being useful knowledge for Motoyasu-san’s future loops too, so it’s not all bad, is it?”
“Well, Gaelion won’t deny that, nano.”
“Speaking of which… this is something that always makes me wonder, but why did Motoyasu-kun end up looping again in the first place?”
This was a question Father and the others often puzzled over as well. In the end, since no answer ever came of it, we didn’t dwell on it too deeply.
“If only I could hit on the right answer with my Accuracy ability, but I honestly have no idea. Even a random guess might not land on the truth.”

Lately, Itsuki had taken to saying all sorts of ridiculous things half-jokingly—that Big Sister was looping me out of revenge, or that I’d been rejected by Filo-tan and was now looping in order to be united with my ideal version of her—infuriating nonsense like that. If Itsuki didn’t knock it off soon, I’d show him a taste of hell in the next loop, I say.
“Maybe Motoyasu ended up like this in the very first world too—went dungeon-crawling, and as a result, picked up another looping weapon. Something like that, maybe.”
Ren chimed in with his own theory. Had something like that ever actually happened? Somehow, it felt off to me.
“Motoyasu-kun’s memories are hazy in a lot of places too. Gaelion-chan, do you have any idea about the period right before or after Motoyasu-kun started looping?”
“All Gaelion can say is that it’s still under investigation, nano. Gaelion’s been diligently keeping records so as to understand it properly, but it often doesn’t go well, nano.”
“…We probably ought to take some kind of countermeasure.”
“Agreed. If there’s something we can do ourselves, it wouldn’t hurt to prepare it in advance. For the sake of our other selves in other loops.”
“We already know that if Motoyasu decides we’re unnecessary, he’ll abandon us without a second thought.”
And with that, Ren and Itsuki began plotting something between themselves.
“Well, in the end it worked out since I got to learn an interesting spell called Four Fairy Morph. Itsuki, did you ever manage to learn Polymorph?”
“Of course I did. Want me to cast it on Naofumi-san? Let’s see… I think the Polymorph that would suit Naofumi-san best would be a cat.”
—Gah! Something like a sharp throb shot through my head. Why on earth would the mere idea of Father undergoing Polymorph give me a headache?
“A cat, huh… that’s not bad, actually.”
“Speaking of cats… who exactly was that cat-like demi-human depicted in that dungeon mural? Was there anyone like that in the historical records?”
“I wonder. Maybe we should ask the queen, or some archaeologist over in Siltvelt? Gaelion-chan, do you know anything?”
“N-nano… Gaelion doesn’t know anything, nano—”

At this, Rival’s behavior turned suspicious in exactly the way it always did when it had something to hide. Somehow, a hazy memory of having seen that figure from the mural before began stirring in the back of my mind.
“Now that I think about it, I recall hearing somewhere that there’s some kind of higher-up that the dragons answer to! Rival!”
“Y-you idiot! If you go and make that person angry, there’s no telling what’ll happen, nano! Learn that there are things in this world scarier than death, nano!”
Rival snapped back at me, clearly flustered.
“Something like being held a grudge against by Motoyasu and getting brutally killed in every single loop, no matter which one?”
“Something like that, nano.”
“If such a person exists, then whatever else happens, I’d really like them to scold Gaelion-san for pulling pranks on us instead of letting us have all the fun.”
“Yeah. Where exactly does this person live, anyway?”
“Such a scary boss… is it a dragon?”

“As for scary—it’s more that their mere existence is frightening, nano. Though… from Gaelion’s own experience meeting them, they’re really not the type to get angry easily, nano. It’s just dragon instinct being afraid—Gaelion doesn’t think the heroes would find them scary at all, nano.”
“I don’t really follow.”
“It’s just that Gaelion and the Dragon Emperor tend to do things that toe a gray line, so that’s why it feels that way, nano. As for personality… they were gentle, nano.”
“…Yeah. I didn’t get the sense they were the type to get angry either, indeed. Only…”
I found myself glancing over at Father. That person… I was certain… certain I’d…
“Motoyasu-kun’s met them too?”
“Indeed… now where was it that I met them, I wonder?”
Was it during the loop? Or before that? It was hazy, buried somewhere in the distant past.
“Well, whatever the case, let’s track this person down and have them scold Gaelion-san and the others properly after exposing all their misdeeds.”

“Gaelion may have done things worth complaining about, but there’s no reason for Gaelion to get scolded, nano! If you’re going to say that, then Gaelion’s going to have Spear Hero’s Filolial boss give him a talking-to too! Gaelion recalls hearing they were in the same world once, nano!”
“There’s something like that too?”
“Filolials have a boss? Who knew.”
“To be precise, it’d be more accurate to call them the boss of all birds, nano. Looks super laid-back, but was actually a real pain to deal with, nano.”
—Gah. As I tried to remember, thinking about Father… along with a violent headache, a certain memory came flooding back to me, I say.
End of the Fluffy Chapter, leading into the Reminiscence Chapter.
